issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path with little on error handling or edge cases such as failed migrations, flush/transaction failures, missing entities, or seeder setup, and the UserSeeder referenced in the seeding command is never defined.

scenarios.name: fix-shared-entitymanager-express
scenarios.rationale: Both wrap requests in RequestContext.create(orm.em, next) and explain the shared identity map and unit of work, but B more directly tells the user to replace the global em constant with orm.em in handlers, while A is thorough but implies the existing em import can stay if it is orm.em, and has a minor import-path quirk.

scenarios.name: soft-delete-and-embedded-address
scenarios.rationale: Both add a nullable deletedAt, an @Filter with deletedAt: null and default: true, an @Embeddable Address, and @Embedded with nullable: true, and both show migration:create then migration:up; A explicitly says to review the generated SQL before applying and describes the expected columns, which matches the rubric closely, while B leads with schema:update --dump and --run and mentions migration:create only as the production path without clearly telling the user to review the generated migration, though its entity code, caveats and extra detail are richer.

scenarios.name: querybuilder-top-authors-driver-import
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric closely: it imports MikroORM and defineConfig from @mikro-orm/postgresql, uses leftJoin, groupBy, orderBy DESC, limit(10) and an admin filter, and says no `type` key is needed. A uses an inner join instead of the required leftJoin and imports defineConfig from the right package in a separate file. It also gives a less direct explanation of the driver import, though its code is otherwise sound.
